title: OpenAI Frees Auto-Review to Cut Manual Agent Approvals
summary:
A new update allows for the automated validation of AI actions in the background to ensure they align with a person's original request. This tool, called Auto-review, is now free for anyone signed in via a ChatGPT account and is accessible through the permissions menu in settings. By deploying a second agent to supervise the primary one, the system removes the requirement for users to manually approve every individual step in a sandbox, aiming to reduce decision fatigue during long tasks without consuming the user's plan usage.

The rollout follows a performance optimization that increased processing speeds by approximately 50% for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol models. These speed gains apply to all partner products using the Sign in With ChatGPT integration, including OpenCode, Pi, Amp, and Devin, and were delivered as part of a sequence of updates starting early October.

selectedTweets.text:
Day 2.1/

We have made Auto-review free for all users signed in through a ChatGPT account. You can enable it in settings > permissions > auto-review. Auto-review improves upon the default sandbox setting that requires you to approve everything, which is prone to decision fatigue unless you spend a lot of time configuring specific rules.

It allows you to run long tasks while having a second agent review all actions taken by the primary agent. Its only goal is to prevent high-risk actions from being taken and to protect against unwanted actions that are not aligned with the original user intent. This  Auto-review feature is now free and does not draw usage from your plan.
